entries.subject: DAMIT 3097: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-3097.txt. Model 3097, version 2019-06-24, pole (77°, -26°), period 13.19055 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 85 ±6 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 80.81 ± 1.24 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 109 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Marciniak et al. (2019), A&A 625, A139
entries.finding: [Marciniak et al. (2019), A&A 625, A139](https://hebe.astro.amu.edu.pl/docs/aa35129-19.pdf) — retained primary publication; see the body-specific selection and calibration above.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 3096, pole ['252', '-49'], [Model 3096](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/3096) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 3096: pole (252°, -49°), 13.19058 h, version 2019-06-24, archive diameter 81 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
